hero.headline: House rejects extension of surveillance law ahead of Friday expiration
hero.body:
The House of Representatives failed to pass a short-term extension of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act on Thursday, clearing the way for the powerful surveillance tool to expire for the first time since its enactment in 2008.

The measure fell short in a 198-218 vote after Democrats announced they would block the renewal in protest of President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Republicans attempted to pass the extension using a fast-track process that required a two-thirds majority, but they fell well short, with 19 members of their own party joining most Democrats in opposition.

Section 702, enacted in the wake of 9/11, allows U.S. intelligence agencies to intercept foreign communications without obtaining individual court warrants. Lawmakers in both parties have long considered it one of the government's most important intelligence tools, yet the political crisis surrounding Pulte's appointment derailed efforts to extend the law.

Democrats cited Pulte's lack of qualifications for the position. "Bill Pulte has no relevant national security experience," said a statement from top House Democrats including Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and the ranking members on the intelligence and judiciary committees. "Consequently, his appointment is in defiance of the law that requires the Director of National Intelligence to have 'extensive' national security experience."

The Democrats also expressed concern about Pulte's willingness to use government databases to search for damaging information on Trump's political opponents. "There is a path to reauthorizing Fisa, but it will require enacting meaningful reforms," the statement said.

Republican leaders in both chambers had been negotiating a compromise to extend Section 702 for three years, involving both Democrats and civil liberties-minded Republicans. Those negotiations collapsed after Trump's announcement of Pulte's appointment.

A similar effort failed in the Senate last week when all Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania opposed the extension, alongside seven conservative Republicans who had raised concerns about the law's civil liberties implications.

However, the expiration of the statute does not mean the surveillance program itself will cease operations. The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court issued a year-long certification authorizing Section 702 collection through approximately March 2027. The law contains a provision allowing collection to continue under that court order even if the underlying statute lapses.

The congressional deadlock ensures Section 702 will lapse on Friday unless Congress takes unexpected action. Republican chairs of the Senate intelligence and judiciary committees have asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio to prepare the administration for a "potential significant gap in foreign intelligence collection."

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as U.S. and Iran Exchange Fire for Second Day
cards.teaser: Oil markets fluctuated sharply after the United States and Iran engaged in military strikes for a second consecutive day.
cards.body:
Oil prices surged as the United States and Iran continued military exchanges for a second consecutive day. Iran responded to U.S. strikes by targeting American assets in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, with damage reported in Bahrain's capital. The escalating conflict has intensified concerns about potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

The ongoing hostilities have created market uncertainty as investors worry about oil production and shipping routes in this strategically vital region. The spike in energy costs is already affecting broader economic pressures, with wholesale inflation rising sharply as the Iran oil shock continues to increase business costs across the economy.

cards.headline: U.S. Wholesale Inflation Rises Sharply as Oil Shock Increases Business Costs
cards.teaser: American wholesale inflation jumped last month as the Iran oil shock continues driving up costs for businesses across sectors.
cards.body:
U.S. wholesale inflation jumped last month as energy prices surge following escalating tensions between the United States and Iran. The spike in producer prices reflects higher costs across transportation, manufacturing, and production sectors, creating broader inflationary pressures throughout the economy.

Oil prices have fluctuated as the two countries exchanged fire, raising concerns about potential open conflict. Meanwhile, the European Central Bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, citing expectations that inflation will run higher than previously forecast while downgrading its economic growth outlook.

cards.headline: Europe Raises Interest Rates as Iran Conflict Drives Inflation Higher
cards.teaser: The European Central Bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, citing hotter inflation expectations driven by the conflict.
cards.body:
The European Central Bank raised its main deposit rate from 2% to 2.25%, marking its first increase since 2023. Financial markets anticipate two additional rate hikes by next spring as the bank responds to inflation pressures stemming from the Iran conflict and resulting energy price surges.

The rate decision reflects deteriorating economic conditions across the eurozone. Inflation has climbed significantly since the conflict began, with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupting energy supplies. The ECB now expects higher inflation than previously forecast while simultaneously downgrading its economic growth projections, creating a challenging environment for policymakers navigating both rising costs and slowing expansion.

cards.headline: Israel Plans Major West Bank Settlement Expansion
cards.teaser: The government is rushing to place temporary housing at about 60 sites before national elections this fall.
cards.body:
Israel is rapidly expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank, planning to place temporary housing at approximately 60 empty sites before national elections this fall. The government is working to install housing infrastructure across multiple locations in the territory.

Human rights groups have raised concerns about the expansion. Amnesty International has accused Israel's government of "ethnic cleansing" of West Bank Palestinians, arguing the Israeli government is deliberately attempting to annex the Palestinian territory.

cards.headline: Ukraine War Surpasses Length of World War I
cards.teaser: The conflict has now lasted longer than the First World War, with parallels in grinding combat and technological changes.
cards.body:
The war in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I, marking a significant milestone in the ongoing conflict. Both wars share striking similarities in their conduct and impact. Entrenched positions, artillery-heavy battles, and high casualty counts characterize both conflicts, which have stretched far longer than many anticipated.

The prolonged fighting has fundamentally transformed Ukrainian society and reshaped the security landscape across Europe. New technologies have played a crucial role in reshaping how warfare is conducted in both conflicts, underscoring how military innovation evolves across different eras.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes Loans for Americans Unable to Pay Medical Bills
cards.teaser: The administration suggested insurers consider lending money to consumers struggling with higher deductibles under health plans.
cards.body:
The Trump administration proposed that insurers consider offering loans to Obamacare consumers who cannot afford higher deductibles, as one-third of Americans carry health care debt. The suggestion comes as the administration grapples with affordability concerns in the insurance marketplace.

The proposal would shift some of the burden of medical costs onto lending arrangements rather than addressing underlying affordability through other policy mechanisms. Critics question whether adding debt obligations helps consumers facing financial strain from medical expenses, while supporters argue it could provide immediate access to needed care.

hero.headline: UK Defense Secretary Resigns Over Military Spending
hero.teaser: John Healey stepped down after saying the government was not investing enough in the British military.
hero.body:
John Healey stepped down as Britain's defense secretary, citing inadequate military spending under Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government. Healey announced his resignation unexpectedly, arguing that current defense funding plans fail to meet the country's security needs.

The departure creates significant challenges for Starmer's leadership, exposing internal divisions over defense priorities and investment levels within the government.

Israel is rapidly expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank, planning to place temporary housing at approximately 60 empty sites before national elections this fall. The government is working to install housing infrastructure across multiple locations in the territory.

cards.headline: El Niño Event Begins, Scientists Warn of Extreme Weather
cards.teaser: US scientists confirmed an El Niño has officially started, raising concerns about temperature increases and weather disruptions.
cards.body:
An El Niño weather event has officially begun, according to US scientists. The natural warming cycle, which forms in the Pacific Ocean, is expected to grow to historic strength and rival or exceed the record El Niño that started in 1997.

Experts warn the event will further heat the planet, which is already warming from fossil fuel pollution, and will likely turbocharge extreme weather worldwide. The 1997 El Niño triggered billions of dollars in damage from heatwaves, floods, droughts, tornadoes, and wildfires.

cards.headline: Protests Threaten World Cup Opening Ceremony in Mexico City
cards.teaser: Unions and other groups plan demonstrations at the stadium as the tournament begins.
cards.body:
Unions and other groups plan to demonstrate at Mexico City's Azteca Stadium during the World Cup opening ceremony. The protests aim to capitalize on the international attention surrounding the tournament's debut.

The demonstrations add complexity to organizing the high-profile event as Mexico co-hosts the World Cup alongside the United States and Canada. Organizers must balance securing the opening ceremony while demonstrators seek to amplify their causes on a global stage.

cards.headline: US Strikes Kill Three Indian Sailors on Oil Tanker
cards.teaser: India lodged a strong protest after its citizens died in an American attack at sea.
cards.body:
Three Indian sailors died when the United States struck an oil tanker in military operations targeting Iranian oil shipments. India lodged strong protests with the US government over the deaths of its crew members.

The incident has created diplomatic tension between Washington and New Delhi, as Indian officials objected to the loss of civilian lives during military operations against commercial vessels. The strike occurred amid escalating US-Iran tensions in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Mexico and Canada Face Tensions in Joint World Cup Hosting
cards.teaser: Despite promoting teamwork, the three North American hosts have experienced significant recent strain in relations.
cards.body:
Mexico and Canada are co-hosting the 2026 World Cup with the United States as part of a historic joint bid that emphasized cooperation among the three nations. The tournament will take place across all three countries, with the final scheduled to be played in the United States.

The partnership comes amid strained diplomatic and economic relations among the North American neighbors. Protests are already planned to disrupt events, including demonstrations at Mexico City's World Cup stadium as the tournament begins, reflecting underlying tensions beneath the surface of the collaborative sporting event.

hero.headline: Opening of Canada-U.S. Bridge Delayed Over Unresolved Issues
hero.body:
The Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario has experienced another delay in its opening, according to recent reporting from AP News and other outlets. The project, which has been under construction for years, was expected to begin operations but officials have postponed the launch without announcing a specific new date.

The bridge represents a significant infrastructure investment designed to improve trade and travel between the United States and Canada. It connects two major metropolitan areas and was intended to serve as an important crossing point for both commercial shipping and passenger traffic across the international border.

The postponement comes as officials work through outstanding issues related to the cross-border project. The specific nature of these unresolved matters has not been publicly disclosed by either the U.S. or Canadian governments. The delay extends a timeline that had already stretched over multiple years of development.

The bridge project has faced increased attention in recent months, with former President Trump previously threatening to block its opening. The nature of Trump's objections and how they relate to the current delay remains unclear from available reporting.

Both American and Canadian officials had prepared for the bridge's debut, and the postponement affects their plans for the facility's opening. The project has been a key piece of infrastructure development intended to enhance connectivity between the two nations.

The bridge is named after hockey legend Gordie Howe and was designed to improve commercial shipping routes and passenger travel options. Its completion would add a major crossing point to the transportation network linking Detroit and Windsor.

Officials from both countries say they are working to address the outstanding matters before announcing a new opening date. The ICC has indicated that reinstatement will depend on meeting specific conditions.

The delay marks another setback for a project that has faced multiple obstacles during its development. The bridge's eventual opening is expected to have significant economic implications for both regions, facilitating increased cross-border commerce and improving travel efficiency between the two countries.

Both governments have expressed commitment to resolving the issues blocking the opening, though the timeline for resolution remains uncertain. The project continues to be closely watched by officials and stakeholders on both sides of the border who anticipate its completion will provide important benefits to the Detroit-Windsor corridor and broader U.S.-Canada trade relations.

cards.headline: Human Remains Found in National Park Identified After 26 Years
cards.teaser: Human remains discovered in a sleeping bag at Olympic National Park have been identified nearly three decades after their discovery.
cards.body:
Authorities have identified human remains that were found in a sleeping bag at Olympic National Park 26 years ago. The remains were discovered in the park nearly three decades ago but went unidentified until recently.

The identification closes a case that remained unsolved for years after the discovery was made at the Washington state park. Officials have now been able to determine the identity of the person whose remains were found.

cards.headline: El Niño Weather Pattern Begins, Scientists Warn of Temperature Extremes
cards.teaser: An El Niño event has officially started according to U.S. scientists, raising concerns about extreme weather and higher temperatures.
cards.body:
U.S. scientists have officially confirmed that an El Niño event is now underway in the Pacific Ocean. The natural warming cycle is expected to grow to historic strength, potentially rivaling or exceeding the record El Niño of 1997.

Experts warn the event will intensify global warming already driven by fossil fuel pollution and turbocharge extreme weather worldwide. The 1997 El Niño triggered billions of dollars in damage from heatwaves, floods, droughts, tornadoes, and wildfires. The current event is forecast to bring similarly severe weather patterns and elevated temperatures across affected regions globally.

cards.headline: Japan Restarts Nuclear Reactor as Waste Storage Space Dwindles
cards.teaser: Japan has restarted a nuclear reactor despite growing concerns about limited storage space for spent nuclear fuel and lack of waste disposal plans.
cards.body:
Japan has restarted a nuclear reactor despite mounting pressure from a critical infrastructure problem: the country is rapidly running out of space to store spent nuclear fuel. This restart brings the waste storage crisis into sharper focus.

The restart exposes a fundamental challenge facing Japan's nuclear program. With storage facilities nearing capacity and no comprehensive disposal plan in place, the country must confront difficult questions about whether its nuclear operations remain viable long-term.

cards.headline: Police Officer, 19, Dies from Crash Injuries
cards.teaser: A 19-year-old police officer has died from injuries sustained in a crash.
cards.body:
Jess Turnbull, a 19-year-old police officer, has died from injuries she sustained in a crash. The chief constable said Turnbull had much to look forward to in both her career and her life.

The young officer's death has been mourned by her department. Turnbull was at the beginning of her law enforcement career when the fatal crash occurred.

cards.headline: Man Jailed for Child Trafficking and Abuse
cards.teaser: Bawan Harwe has been sentenced to prison for a series of child abuse offenses against girls aged 12 to 16.
cards.body:
Bawan Harwe has been jailed for trafficking and abusing girls. He was sentenced for a series of child abuse offenses committed against victims between the ages of 12 and 16.

The case involved multiple young victims over a period of time. Harwe was convicted on charges related to both trafficking and abuse of the underage girls.

cards.headline: Asylum Appeal Backlog Reaches Record High
cards.teaser: New figures show the backlog of asylum appeals has reached a record high, even as initial case backlogs have been reduced.
cards.body:
The number of asylum appeals has surged to record levels, according to newly released figures. This represents a significant shift in the asylum system, as the government has managed to reduce the backlog of initial applications awaiting decisions.

The data highlights where bottlenecks now exist within the process. While authorities have improved their handling of first-stage cases, the appeals stage has become increasingly congested, creating delays for those seeking to challenge asylum decisions.

hero.teaser: The European Central Bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, citing hotter inflation expectations driven by the conflict.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Draws Over $70 Billion in Retail Orders
cards.teaser: The space company's public offering has generated more than $70 billion in retail investor orders ahead of its market debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for a record-breaking initial public offering, aiming to raise $75 billion. The company, which recently merged with xAI, has attracted massive retail investor interest with over $70 billion in orders for its shares.

The IPO marks the first of three anticipated mega-offerings from AI companies this year. Wall Street firms have begun issuing their initial stock recommendations as SpaceX moves toward its market debut.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes Loans for Americans Unable to Pay Medical Bills
cards.teaser: The administration suggested insurers consider lending money to consumers struggling with higher deductibles under health plans.
cards.body:
The Trump administration proposed that insurers consider offering loans to Obamacare consumers who cannot afford higher deductibles, as one-third of Americans carry health care debt. The suggestion comes as the administration grapples with affordability concerns in the insurance marketplace.

The proposal would shift some of the burden of medical costs onto lending arrangements rather than addressing underlying affordability through other policy mechanisms. Critics question whether adding debt obligations helps consumers facing financial strain from medical expenses, while supporters argue it could provide immediate access to needed care.

cards.headline: FDA Approves New Sunscreen Ingredient Used in Europe and Asia
cards.teaser: The Food and Drug Administration approved a sunscreen ingredient widely used abroad, marking a significant regulatory shift.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration approved a new sunscreen ingredient that has been used in Europe and Asia for years, representing a meaningful advance in sun protection options available to American consumers. Dermatologists called the approval a significant step forward for skin cancer prevention.

The ingredient had faced years of regulatory review before gaining FDA clearance. American sunscreen formulations have lagged behind international options due to the lengthy approval process for new active ingredients, leaving consumers with fewer effective choices for sun protection compared to those available in other developed countries.

cards.headline: Lee Raymond, Former Exxon Mobil Chief Executive, Dies at 87
cards.teaser: The oil executive who oversaw the creation of Exxon Mobil through a major acquisition has died.
cards.body:
Lee Raymond, who created the global oil giant Exxon Mobil through an acquisition and led the company for years, died at 87. He oversaw Exxon's acquisition of a rival company and implemented extensive cost-cutting measures during his tenure.

Raymond was known for his aggressive business strategy and his public denial of the scientific consensus on climate change during his time leading one of the world's largest oil companies. His leadership shaped the modern energy industry and established Exxon Mobil as a dominant force in global petroleum markets.

hero.headline: DoorDash launches AI chatbot for natural language food ordering
hero.body:
DoorDash has introduced Ask DoorDash, an artificial intelligence chatbot that enables users to place food orders using conversational language and photos rather than manually navigating restaurant menus. The feature represents a significant change in how the delivery platform handles customer interactions.

The chatbot allows users to describe what they want to eat in their own words instead of scrolling through individual restaurants and manually building a cart. Users can also upload photos to help the AI identify specific dishes or food types they are seeking. The technology interprets natural language requests and matches them to available menu items from DoorDash's network of restaurants and stores.

Food delivery platforms have traditionally required customers to browse restaurant listings, search through menus, and manually add items one by one. Ask DoorDash attempts to simplify this process by allowing users to describe their preferences, dietary needs, or cravings and receive relevant recommendations. This approach addresses what some in the industry describe as "choice overload," where the sheer number of available options makes decision-making difficult for consumers.

The chatbot could particularly benefit users who know what they want to eat but do not have a specific restaurant in mind. By accepting photo inputs, the feature may also help users reorder dishes they have seen elsewhere or identify menu items based on visual appearance rather than written descriptions. The photo functionality adds another layer of convenience to the ordering experience.

This launch reflects a broader industry trend toward conversational AI tools in consumer applications. Other delivery platforms are exploring similar AI-driven search and recommendation features as competition intensifies in the food delivery market. DoorDash competes with Uber Eats and other services that are testing comparable technologies.

Just Eat, a delivery company operating in 16 countries, recently launched a similar initiative by introducing a voice-activated AI assistant in its UK app. That assistant, described as a "personal food concierge," uses conversational abilities to provide tailored recommendations. The company emphasized that the voice feature also enhances accessibility for users with mobility or visual impairments. Just Eat's voice assistant can communicate in dozens of languages and offers personalized accent options.

The broader adoption of AI in food delivery suggests that companies see significant opportunities to streamline the ordering process and improve user satisfaction. By reducing the friction between deciding what to eat and completing an order, these platforms aim to increase transaction volume and customer loyalty.

DoorDash has not yet disclosed which AI model powers Ask DoorDash or outlined specific plans for expanding the feature's capabilities. As the company rolls out this technology, it will likely provide insight into how AI-driven ordering experiences shape the future of food delivery services.

cards.headline: South Korea fines Coupang over $400 million for data breach affecting millions
cards.teaser: South Korean authorities issued a record fine following a breach that compromised the personal information of over 30 million customers.
cards.body:
South Korean regulators fined e-commerce giant Coupang over $400 million for a data breach affecting more than 30 million customers. The penalty marks a record-breaking enforcement action by South Korean authorities against a cybersecurity incident.

The breach exposed personal information of a substantial portion of South Korea's population. Investigators found that Coupang's data protection measures were inadequate, allowing the compromise to occur.

cards.headline: SpaceX satellites creating unintended geoengineering experiment
cards.teaser: The growing constellation of SpaceX satellites orbiting Earth is producing effects researchers are characterizing as an accidental geoengineering experiment.
cards.body:
SpaceX's expanding network of satellites is generating environmental effects that scientists are describing as an unplanned geoengineering experiment. The satellites, deployed as part of the company's internet service infrastructure, are having observable impacts on Earth's atmosphere and space environment.

Researchers are studying the cumulative effects of thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit. The satellite constellation has grown rapidly in recent years as SpaceX works to provide global internet coverage. Scientists are monitoring how the satellites interact with the upper atmosphere and whether they produce measurable changes to Earth systems.

cards.headline: Endurance Energy raises $54 million to develop ocean geothermal power
cards.teaser: A company founded by SpaceX veterans secured funding to tap geothermal energy from the ocean floor.
cards.body:
Endurance Energy raised $54 million to develop technology that harnesses geothermal energy from beneath the ocean. The company, founded by former SpaceX engineer Andrew Redd, aims to access what it describes as vast amounts of untapped energy stored in underwater geothermal sources.

The funding round will support development of systems to extract heat from ocean floor geothermal reservoirs. Redd's background includes work on SpaceX projects before launching the energy venture. The company believes ocean-based geothermal resources represent a significant opportunity for renewable energy generation that has received limited attention compared to land-based geothermal systems.

cards.headline: El Niño climate pattern begins, raising risk of temperature extremes
cards.teaser: US scientists confirmed that an El Niño event has officially started, increasing the likelihood of extreme weather and higher global temperatures.
cards.body:
An El Niño event has officially started, according to US scientists, triggering concerns about extreme weather and elevated global temperatures in the months ahead. The natural climate pattern involves periodic warming of Pacific Ocean waters that influences weather systems worldwide.

El Niño typically causes higher global average temperatures and disrupts normal precipitation patterns across regions. The phenomenon can intensify droughts in some areas while triggering heavy rainfall in others, depending on location. Scientists expect these effects to persist through the end of the year.

cards.headline: National Science Foundation decommissions Alaska ocean monitoring network
cards.teaser: The National Science Foundation is shutting down an ocean monitoring network that provides critical data to Alaska's fishing industry and coastal communities.
cards.body:
The National Science Foundation is decommissioning an ocean monitoring network that Alaska's fishing industry and coastal communities rely on for environmental data. The shutdown will eliminate access to real-time information about ocean conditions that affect commercial fishing operations worth billions of dollars annually.

The monitoring network tracked ocean temperatures, currents, and other environmental factors used by fishermen and community planners along Alaska's coastline. Fishing operations depend on this data to make decisions about when and where to deploy vessels. Coastal communities also use the information to prepare for changing ocean conditions that could affect infrastructure and safety.

cards.headline: Research reveals complex gene transfers shaped early cellular evolution
cards.teaser: Scientists found that the first complex cells acquired genes through multiple waves of transfers from different species.
cards.body:
New research shows that early complex cells developed through successive waves of gene transfers from multiple species, revealing a more intricate evolutionary history than previously understood. The findings describe how ancestral genomes were assembled from genetic material originating in diverse organisms.

The study examined the genetic makeup of early eukaryotic cells, which contain complex internal structures unlike simpler bacterial cells. Researchers traced how genes from various sources became incorporated into these ancestral genomes over time. The pattern suggests that horizontal gene transfer played a larger role in early cellular evolution than vertical inheritance alone.

hero.headline: Knicks rally from 29 points down to stun Spurs in Game 4, move within one win of title
hero.body:
The New York Knicks completed one of the most remarkable comebacks in NBA Finals history, erasing a 29-point second-half deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4. The victory pushed the Knicks within one win of securing their first championship in more than 50 years.

OG Anunoby delivered the decisive play with a tip-in that sealed the historic comeback and sent the Madison Square Garden crowd into celebration. The moment instantly entered Knicks lore as one of the franchise's most memorable plays. The improbable rally marked one of the largest comebacks in Finals history and shifted momentum decisively in the series.

The Knicks trailed by 29 points in the second half before mounting their furious charge. The team's defense tightened considerably in the final period while their offense found rhythm after struggling through much of the first half. The comeback required contributions across the roster as New York chipped away at the seemingly insurmountable lead.

The victory puts the Knicks in position to clinch their first NBA title since 1973. The franchise has endured decades of playoff disappointments and near-misses, making this Finals run particularly significant for longtime fans. One more victory would end the 53-year championship drought that has defined the modern era of Knicks basketball.

The Spurs now face elimination after holding what appeared to be a commanding advantage. San Antonio led comfortably for most of the game before the collapse in the final period. The team will need to regroup quickly to extend the series and prevent the Knicks from celebrating a championship on their home court in the next game.

cards.headline: Manchester City's second bid for Elliot Anderson rejected by Nottingham Forest
cards.teaser: Nottingham Forest turned down Manchester City's second offer for midfielder Elliot Anderson, reportedly worth 120 million pounds.
cards.body:
Nottingham Forest has rejected Manchester City's second bid for midfielder Elliot Anderson, which was valued at £120 million. Despite the rejection, City remains interested in pursuing the player.

Should Forest agree to sell Anderson, the midfielder would prefer to join Manchester City over Manchester United, who also hold interest in the 21-year-old.

cards.headline: Dan Evans to retire from tennis after Wimbledon
cards.teaser: Former British number one Dan Evans announced he will retire from professional tennis following this year's Wimbledon tournament.
cards.body:
Dan Evans will end his professional tennis career after competing at Wimbledon this year. The former British number one made the announcement about his retirement plans.

Evans reached the top of British tennis rankings during his career. Wimbledon will serve as his final tournament before stepping away from professional competition. The timing allows him to finish his career at the sport's most prestigious grass-court event in his home country.

cards.headline: Somali referee Omar Artan appointed to UEFA Super Cup after World Cup snub
cards.teaser: Omar Artan will referee the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa after being left off the World Cup officiating roster.
cards.body:
Somali referee Omar Artan has been appointed to officiate the UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa this summer. The appointment comes despite Artan missing out on selection for the World Cup officiating team.

The Super Cup, which matches the winners of the Champions League and Europa League, represents a significant assignment and reflects UEFA's confidence in Artan's abilities as an official.

cards.headline: Kimi Antonelli says he has more to prove despite commanding championship lead
cards.teaser: Driver Kimi Antonelli maintains he still needs to answer questions about his ability despite building a substantial championship lead through six races.
cards.body:
Kimi Antonelli says he still has questions to answer despite establishing an imposing championship lead after just six races this season.

The driver holds a commanding position in the standings but remains focused on proving himself further. Antonelli believes there is still much he needs to demonstrate as the season progresses.

cards.headline: World Cup 2026 set to be largest and loudest edition of tournament
cards.teaser: The 2026 World Cup will feature an expanded format with more teams and matches than any previous edition of the tournament.
cards.body:
The 2026 World Cup represents a significant departure from previous tournaments in scale and scope. The competition will feature more teams and matches than any World Cup in history, spread across multiple host nations in North America.

The expanded format marks a new era for international soccer's premier event. The tournament's larger size will bring the World Cup to more cities and fans than ever before. Organizers have positioned this edition as bigger and more accessible than previous iterations of the competition.

cards.headline: MLB power rankings show movement outside top five teams
cards.teaser: The top five teams in Major League Baseball power rankings remained unchanged for the fourth consecutive week, but significant shifts occurred throughout the rest of the list.
cards.body:
The top five teams in MLB power rankings remained unchanged for the fourth consecutive week, demonstrating stability among the league's elite clubs. Beyond this tier, however, significant movement occurred throughout the rest of the rankings as teams either gained or lost ground.

This volatility in the middle and lower portions of the rankings reflects the competitive nature of the season as clubs battle for playoff positioning across both leagues.

hero.headline: J.D. Vance to Appear on The View to Discuss Faith Memoir
hero.body:
Vice President J.D. Vance will appear on ABC's The View on June 16 to discuss his upcoming memoir about his spiritual journey. The book, titled Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith, will be published the same day by HarperCollins.

Vance announced the memoir through social media, saying he had worked on the project "for a long time." According to the publisher's description, the book is "a spiritual exploration of what it means to be a Christian across the seasons of Vance's life" and documents his loss of faith and eventual return to Christianity.

The Vice President converted to Catholicism in 2019 at age 35, after growing up in a loosely evangelical family. The memoir explores how his faith now guides his work in public life and informs his vision for the future.

The timing of the book release reflects broader patterns in American politics. Several potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidates, including Vice President Kamala Harris and governors Gavin Newsom, Andy Beshear, and Josh Shapiro, have recently released or announced memoirs. Political observers increasingly view Vance as an early frontrunner for the 2028 Republican nomination.

Vance's emphasis on faith has become increasingly central to his political identity. His Catholic conversion has shaped his positions on abortion and family policy. He has previously justified the White House's deportation policies through his interpretation of Catholicism, invoking the concept of "ordo amoris" or "order of love" to argue for prioritizing obligations to fellow citizens over outsiders.

Those religious interpretations have drawn criticism from Vatican officials. Before becoming Pope Leo XIV in May 2025, a social media account apparently belonging to him shared criticism of the White House's deportation plans. Without mentioning Vance directly, the late Pope Francis argued in a letter that the true "order of love" should be discovered through reflection on the parable of the Good Samaritan, promoting love that builds "a fraternity open to all, without exception."

Communion follows the success of Vance's first memoir, Hillbilly Elegy: A Memoir of a Family and Culture in Crisis, published in 2016. That book chronicled his upbringing in rural Ohio and his path from a troubled family background to Yale Law School. It became a major bestseller, spending more than 200 weeks on the New York Times bestseller list and selling more than five million copies worldwide. Ron Howard later adapted the book into a film starring Glenn Close and Amy Adams.

The View appearance represents a significant media platform for Vance to reach audiences beyond traditional conservative outlets, with millions of viewers tuning in daily to the program.

cards.headline: Helen Mirren Discusses Recent Verbal Attack in London
cards.teaser: The actress addressed being called an evil Zionist bitch during an incident in London in late May.
cards.body:
Helen Mirren spoke publicly about a recent verbal attack she suffered in London, where a man called her an evil Zionist bitch. The actress, currently in Sicily receiving a Taormina Film Festival Lifetime Achievement Award, addressed the incident during festival appearances. In late May, Mirren had expressed support for her MobLand co-star Tom Hardy.

During her remarks in Sicily, Mirren questioned the logic behind repeating historical injustices, asking how people could repeat the actions of what was done to them. The actress also discussed her working relationship with Hardy during the festival's events. The verbal attack in London occurred in public, adding to ongoing discussions about public harassment and political speech.

cards.headline: Nick Cave Performs Shane MacGowan Tribute in Ireland
cards.teaser: The Bad Seeds played A Rainy Night in Soho and several rarities including the first performance of Stranger Than Kindness in over a decade.
cards.body:
Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds performed a tribute to Shane MacGowan in Ireland, singing the soulful A Rainy Night in Soho. The concert included several rarely performed songs from the band's catalog, marking special moments for longtime fans. The setlist featured unexpected choices that showcased the depth of Cave's musical archive.

Among the rarities was Stranger Than Kindness, which the band performed for the first time in more than a decade. The song's return to the live repertoire highlighted Cave's willingness to revisit older material during the Irish shows. The MacGowan tribute carried particular emotional weight, honoring the late Pogues frontman's legacy in his home country.

cards.headline: Nintendo Unveils Ocarina of Time Remake and New Kingdom Hearts Game
cards.teaser: The latest Nintendo Direct revealed updates for Switch 2 including a modified version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and a new Kingdom Hearts title.
cards.body:
Nintendo's latest Direct presentation revealed information about upcoming games for the Nintendo Switch 2 and Switch systems. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be modified for the Nintendo Switch 2, bringing the classic game to the new hardware. The presentation also announced the return of the Kingdom Hearts series, the action RPG collaboration between Disney and Square Enix.

The Direct included reveals of new titles alongside updates to existing games. The Ocarina of Time remake represents one of the most anticipated announcements, as the original Nintendo 64 game remains one of the most beloved entries in the Zelda franchise. The Kingdom Hearts reveal signals continued support for major third-party franchises on Nintendo platforms.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Says She Nearly Had Anxiety Attack Before Glastonbury
cards.teaser: The singer discussed the intense emotions she experienced before her headlining set at the iconic UK festival.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo revealed she nearly experienced an anxiety attack before taking the stage for her headlining performance at Glastonbury. The singer opened up about the intense pressure she felt before performing at one of the world's most famous music festivals. Despite the pre-show nerves, Rodrigo described the experience as transformative once she began performing.

Rodrigo reflected on how music's power transcended her anxiety during the performance. She described the moments on stage as magical and beyond description, highlighting how the experience reinforced her connection to performing. The Glastonbury headline slot represented a major milestone in Rodrigo's career, placing her among the festival's most prominent performers.

cards.headline: Shaboozey Reflects on A Bar Song (Tipsy) Success
cards.teaser: The country star discussed realizing his song was climbing the charts and will release a new album in July.
cards.body:
Shaboozey discussed the moment he realized his song A Bar Song (Tipsy) was becoming a major hit. The country artist said the track kept climbing and he rode the wave of its success. The song's popularity marked a breakthrough moment in Shaboozey's career, expanding his audience significantly.

The artist announced his new album The Outlaw Cherie Lee Other Western Tales will be released in July. The upcoming project follows the success of A Bar Song (Tipsy) and represents his next major release. Shaboozey's comments reflected his approach to handling sudden fame and chart success.

cards.headline: Mean Girls Musical Cancels Belfast Shows Following City Violence
cards.teaser: An actor from the production said they have not left their house and are scared following disorder in Belfast.
cards.body:
The Mean Girls musical canceled its Belfast run following violence and disorder in the city. A cast member from the production stated they had not left their house and were scared due to the situation. The cancellation affected multiple scheduled performances at the Belfast venue.

The disorder in Belfast prompted safety concerns for cast and crew members, leading to the decision to cancel the shows. The actor's comments reflected the tense atmosphere surrounding the production's planned performances. The musical's producers prioritized safety in making the decision to pull the Belfast dates.

hero.headline: House rejects extension of surveillance law ahead of Friday expiration
hero.body:
The House of Representatives failed to pass a short-term extension of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act on Thursday, clearing the way for the powerful surveillance tool to expire for the first time since its enactment in 2008.

The measure fell short in a 198-218 vote after Democrats announced they would block the renewal in protest of President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Republicans attempted to pass the extension using a fast-track process that required a two-thirds majority, but they fell well short, with 19 members of their own party joining most Democrats in opposition.

Section 702, enacted in the wake of 9/11, allows U.S. intelligence agencies to intercept foreign communications without obtaining individual court warrants. Lawmakers in both parties have long considered it one of the government's most important intelligence tools, yet the political crisis surrounding Pulte's appointment derailed efforts to extend the law.

Democrats cited Pulte's lack of qualifications for the position. "Bill Pulte has no relevant national security experience," said a statement from top House Democrats including Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and the ranking members on the intelligence and judiciary committees. "Consequently, his appointment is in defiance of the law that requires the Director of National Intelligence to have 'extensive' national security experience."

The Democrats also expressed concern about Pulte's willingness to use government databases to search for damaging information on Trump's political opponents. "There is a path to reauthorizing Fisa, but it will require enacting meaningful reforms," the statement said.

Republican leaders in both chambers had been negotiating a compromise to extend Section 702 for three years, involving both Democrats and civil liberties-minded Republicans. Those negotiations collapsed after Trump's announcement of Pulte's appointment.

A similar effort failed in the Senate last week when all Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania opposed the extension, alongside seven conservative Republicans who had raised concerns about the law's civil liberties implications.

However, the expiration of the statute does not mean the surveillance program itself will cease operations. The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court issued a year-long certification authorizing Section 702 collection through approximately March 2027. The law contains a provision allowing collection to continue under that court order even if the underlying statute lapses.

The congressional deadlock ensures Section 702 will lapse on Friday unless Congress takes unexpected action. Republican chairs of the Senate intelligence and judiciary committees have asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio to prepare the administration for a "potential significant gap in foreign intelligence collection."

cards.headline: House Republicans meet with Hegseth after Trump calls for Pentagon funding in next bill
cards.teaser: The meeting follows the president's demand that the next party-line package include increased Pentagon funding and the SAVE America Act.
cards.body:
House Republicans met with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as lawmakers prepare to draft party-line legislation. President Trump has called for the next reconciliation package to include substantial Pentagon funding and the SAVE America Act.

The reconciliation process allows certain legislation to pass the Senate with a simple majority, giving Republicans a pathway to advance their priorities with limited Democratic input. Trump's request signals his administration's emphasis on increased defense spending in the coming budget negotiations.

cards.headline: Anthropic CEO calls for government power to block unsafe AI deployments
cards.teaser: Dario Amodei argues governments should have authority to prevent artificial intelligence deployments that fail to meet safety standards.
cards.body:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay arguing governments should have the power to block dangerous deployments of artificial intelligence if they do not meet safety standards. The assertion builds on the company's approach to AI safety, which has created tensions with competitors.

Amodei released the essay on his website Wednesday. The position represents a pro-regulation stance in the ongoing debate over AI governance and puts Anthropic at odds with other technology companies.

cards.headline: White House UFC event cost at least $60 million
cards.teaser: Federal agencies and the UFC are spending at least $60 million on the cage fight scheduled for the White House South Lawn on Sunday.
cards.body:
Federal agencies and the Ultimate Fighting Championship are spending at least $60 million to stage a cage fight at the White House on Sunday, which is President Trump's birthday. The funds covered building an octagon fighting arena on the South Lawn and purchasing and delivering food.

A recent poll found only 16 percent of Americans said it was appropriate for President Trump to host the UFC event at the White House. Another 46 percent opposed the event, according to the Reuters/Ipsos survey.

cards.headline: FDA authorizes emergency use of generic screwworm drug for pets
cards.teaser: The agency approved the first generic over-the-counter tablet to treat New World screwworm in dogs and cats as cases emerge in livestock.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration granted emergency use authorization to a generic over-the-counter tablet to treat New World screwworm in dogs and cats. The authorization represents the first generic animal drug approved for use against the parasite.

The decision comes as officials in Texas and New Mexico confirmed at least seven cases of screwworm in cattle. The parasite poses a threat to both livestock and domestic animals in affected regions.

cards.headline: CDC chief says USAID cuts did not hamper Ebola response
cards.teaser: Acting CDC director Jay Bhattacharya denied that Trump administration foreign aid cuts negatively affected the global response to the ongoing outbreak.
cards.body:
The acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention denied that the Trump administration's cuts to foreign aid negatively impacted the global response to the Ebola outbreak. The CDC chief stated there is "no evidence" that the reduced funding hampered international health efforts.

During an appearance on NewsNation's Elizabeth Vargas Reports, the official praised the professionals involved in the response, describing them as a competent and committed group dedicated to addressing the outbreak.

cards.headline: Hegseth dismisses question about potential Iran strike as war crime
cards.teaser: The Defense Secretary criticized a reporter's question about whether a U.S. strike on Iranian civilian infrastructure would constitute a war crime.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected a reporter's question about whether a U.S. strike on Iran's civilian infrastructure would constitute a war crime, calling it disingenuous. He argued the question unfairly questioned the motives of military professionals.

The exchange occurred Wednesday amid escalating U.S.-Iran tensions. Hegseth emphasized that American military personnel maintain high professional standards.
